title: Nine Thrones: keeping local AI NPC dialogue tied to the actual game world
author: RedTowerDev
selftext:
Development-build screenshot: Baroness Isolde responding through the optional local Qwen3.5 4B dialogue system.



Hi everyone! We're Red Tower Studios, and Nine Thrones, our party-based fantasy RPG with tactical turn-based combat, has just entered Early Access on Steam.



One development problem we've focused on is giving NPCs room to speak naturally while keeping their dialogue connected to what actually happened in the game.



Our optional offline dialogue uses Qwen3.5 4B and 9B. We build character prompts from identity, personality, the current situation, relationships, and relevant recorded knowledge. The prompt distinguishes firsthand knowledge from unconfirmed reports.



The dialogue pipeline includes checks for unsupported factual claims. Game systems remain responsible for actual changes to the world: an NPC saying something happened doesn't make it a completed game event.



A small example from our prompt design: when a player asks for a joke, we encourage present-tense wordplay instead of invented personal anecdotes. The aim is to leave room for personality while reducing opportunities to manufacture a past event. This is an ongoing development problem, not something we're claiming to have solved perfectly.



Traditional authored conversations remain alongside the optional AI dialogue. We also use generative AI in our art workflow, which typically moves from owner-directed ChatGPT images through Procreate edits and our in-game tools.



Nine Thrones is a paid Early Access game, with more work ahead on the world and simulation:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5093250/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5093250/)



For others building NPC dialogue: how do you keep generated conversation consistent with a character's recorded memories without making every reply overly cautious?

comments.author: ArtificialBeingsInc
comments.body: One test might be to give the NPC the same memory but change its relationship to the player: friendly, annoyed, then suspicious. The facts should stay consistent while the warmth and willingness to share change. I’d also test a false belief recorded in the character’s own knowledge: can they state it confidently without the game treating it as world truth? That would let them have personality without forcing every line to sound like a cautious witness.
